record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: What are the precise differential cross sections of electrons emitted in charged-current neutrino interactions on lead, and can such measurements provide reliable information about neutrino temperatures at emission if a core-collapse supernova occurs?

evidence.quote: Lead represent an interesting nucleus as well, e.g. for supernova observatories [20,21,22,23,24]. In this context, the precise measurement of the differential cross sections of electrons emitted in charge-current events would be very useful, since their measurement would give us precious information on the neutrino temperatures at emission, if a core-collapse supernova explodes [23].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current neutrino reactions on a lead target,
  ν_e + ^{208}Pb → e^- + ^{208}Bi^*,
the excited bismuth nucleus subsequently de-exciting by emission of one or more neutrons. Assume an incoming electron-neutrino flux whose energy spectrum is parameterized by a Fermi–Dirac (or pinched thermal) distribution
  f(E_ν; T, η) ∝ E_ν^2 / (1 + exp(E_ν/T − η)),
characterized by a temperature T (and, optionally, a pinching parameter η) appropriate to the neutrinosphere of a core-collapse supernova.

(a) Derive, from a microscopic nuclear-structure model of ^{208}Pb (e.g. QRPA or shell-model treatment of the allowed Fermi and Gamow–Teller strengths together with forbidden multipoles), the doubly differential cross section
  d^2σ / (dE_e dcosθ_e)
for the outgoing electron, as a function of the incident neutrino energy E_ν, the electron kinetic energy E_e, and the electron emission angle θ_e, including Coulomb corrections (Fermi function or effective momentum approximation) for the outgoing electron in the field of the daughter nucleus.

(b) Determine the corresponding singly differential spectrum dσ/dE_e after folding with the supernova neutrino flux f(E_ν; T, η), and quantify its sensitivity to the temperature parameter T. In particular, identify observables built from the electron spectrum (for example moments ⟨E_e⟩, ⟨E_e^2⟩, or ratios of partial cross sections leading to one-neutron and two-neutron emission channels) that allow a reliable reconstruction of T from the measured electron differential cross sections in the event of a galactic core-collapse supernova, and estimate the precision with which T can be inferred given realistic detector energy resolution and statistics.
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical estimates of charged-current neutrino-^{208}Pb cross sections have been computed in QRPA and shell-model frameworks (e.g., Engel–Fuller–Vogel; Volpe et al.; Paar et al.; Almosly et al., 2016), and the HALO detector at SNOLAB exploits 1n/2n branching ratios as a temperature diagnostic. However, precise differential cross sections remain model-dependent (no direct experimental measurement of CC ν_e on ^{208}Pb exists), and the achievable precision on supernova neutrino temperatures from such measurements is still under active investigation (HALO-1kT, theoretical updates). The problem is therefore partially solved.

status_evidence.title: HALO, a supernova neutrino observatory
status_evidence.snippet: HALO observes supernova neutrino interactions via ejected final-state neutrons from charged-current νe interactions on lead; the 1n/2n ratio is sensitive to neutrino temperature.
status_evidence.claim: HALO uses CC ν_e–Pb interactions and the 1n/2n ratio is sensitive to neutrino temperature.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical estimates of supernova-neutrino cross sections for the stable even-even lead isotopes: Charged-current reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical (QRPA/shell-model) estimates of CC supernova-neutrino cross sections for even-even Pb isotopes.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical cross sections exist but are model dependent and not directly experimentally validated.

status_evidence.title: HALO – the Helium and Lead Observatory
status_evidence.snippet: 76 tonnes of lead with 3He neutron counters; neutron-burst signature of a supernova.
status_evidence.claim: HALO infrastructure is built to exploit these cross sections for supernova detection.
